labs.objective: to set up tools for the semester and to read through the syllabus.

labs.objective: to write short programs involving output and the turtle library and submit those to the Gradescope.

labs.title: Lab 2: Strings & Loops
labs.objective: to input and manipulate strings, as well as looping through lists and strings.

labs.title: Lab 3: Representing Colors & Manipulating Images
labs.objective: to use the three different formats for colors (name, RGB & hexadecimal) and manipulate images using standard libraries.

labs.title: Lab 4: Getting Input & Decisions
labs.objective: to use decisions to manipulate images and lists (list comprehension) as well as get user input.

labs.title: Lab 5: Logical Expressions & Circuits
labs.objective: to translate between logical expressions and circuits, as well as understand binary numbers.

labs.title: Lab 6: Pandas & Github
labs.objective: to use the pandas library to read in CSV files, manipulate columns, and plot data, as well as be familiar with GitHub.

labs.title: Lab 7: NYC OpenData & Functions
labs.objective: to obtain and analyze NYC OpenData using pandas and to write stand-alone programs with functions.

labs.title: Lab 8: Top Down Design & Dictionaries
labs.objective: to write programs in a top-down design fashion and use dictionaries.

labs.title: Lab 9: Spatial Maps & Code Quality
labs.objective: to create spatial maps and improve debugging skills.

labs.title: Lab 10: Indefinite Loops & Random Numbers
labs.objective: to use indefinite loops in programs and understand canonical Unix tools (git and vi).

labs.title: Lab 11: Machine Language and Unix Pipes
labs.objective: to write simple machine language programs (MIPS) & link shell commands using pipes.

labs.title: Lab 12: Getting Started with C++
labs.objective: to write C++ programs with I/O, variables and definite loops and list file types in Unix.

labs.title: Lab 13: C++ Decisions & Indefinite Loops
labs.objective: to write C++ programs that using decisions and while loops and use shell commands to find versions and documentation.

coursework.extraCredit: There is up to 15% extra credit for completing the quiz and code review before the due date: 5% for 1 day early, 10% for 2 days early, and 15% for 3 or more days early.
coursework.codeReview: Code Reviews; There will also be weekly walk-throughs ("code reviews") where you explain one of the programs you wrote for homework to a teaching assistant. Code reviews are integral to software design and development: explaining your coding decisions and convincing another it works correctly leads to improvements in the design and lessens unexpected behaviors and errors. Code reviews are offered on weekdays, when classes are in session, in lab 1001E HN. First priority is given to those with appointments (available on Navigate) and then walk-ins. Each week focuses on program that you wrote the previous week (see calendar for programs). Using IDLE, you code up the program from scratch. As you're doing this, you guide the teaching assistant through your design and development.; If something is unclear or you are stuck, ask questions! Having a two-way conversation about the concepts, the code, and the design are highly encouraged. After you successfully code and run your program, the teaching assistant will ask you to modify it (a very common part of technical interviews).; There are no make-up code reviews. Instead, the top 10 scores are used to compute your quiz grade. Extra credit
coursework.quizzes: Written Quizzes; Each week, there will be a paper quiz on the lecture notes, reading, submitted programs, and online lab exercises. Quiz questions will cover the topics from lectures, labs, and homework. Quizzes are offered on weekdays, when classes are in session, in lab 1001E HN. First priority is given to those with appointments (available on Navigate) and then walk-ins. There are no make-up quizzes. Instead, the top 10 scores are used to compute your quiz grade. Extra credit (up to 15%) is available for completing quizzes by the target date. See calendar for dates.; The quizzes are on paper, and you December not use any notes, books, or any computer device (laptop, phone, calculator, smart watch, etc.).
